messages.author: 7a5ec8c33022cdf8
messages.subject: Likelihood Functions
parts:
Hi

I was wondering if there is way to extract the probabilities for each category of a particular item across a multiple dimensions? 

I have a three factor nominal model and I would like to see the likelihoods associated with the different answers to a single question for each factor. I've tried the probtrace function as well as iteminfo, but it gives me a total probability. Is there a way to separate it into the different factors? I want to understand the most likely answers under different factors. 

Thank you!
Leigh

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Likelihood Functions
parts:
No, this is not possible. Multidimensional IRT models are fitted jointly, so isolating the individual factor contributions is not possible. This would be analogous to trying to isolate the IVs in a linear regression model with multiple predictor variables --- at best, you could get a partial representation in the system, but this largely what is meant by the slopes themselves (the slope parameters in IRT are of course no different). And because of the bounded nature in the expected values, E(y| θ​​, ψ​​), the behaviour of the expected values is always contingent upon the remainder of the values in the system. 

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Likelihood Functions
parts:
The highest numerical value is treated as the highest category for each respective item (easy-peasy interpretation that way). This is true even if you coded your binary items as 10-10000...mirt just re-codes these to something it's more used to seeing, so the actual values used to code items is generally irrelevant. 

Phil
